skill: Electric guitar technique with pentatonic scales and loop pedal usage

tracks.name: Foundations: Pentatonic mastery and looping basics
tracks.identity_statement: I establish clean technique, map pentatonic patterns across two positions, and create a simple loop to accompany blues ideas.
tracks.intended_outcome: Can play pentatonic shapes in two positions with clean tone and basic loop track to accompany blues ideas.
tracks.rationale: Establishes a solid foundation: pentatonic shapes, two-position fluency, and the ability to create a simple loop for blues context before introducing more complex looping and improvisation.

tracks.name: Blues improvisation over loop
tracks.identity_statement: I improvise blues phrases over a looped backing using pentatonic shapes, apply muting and voice-leading, and maintain key.
tracks.intended_outcome: Can improvise 8–12 bar blues melodies over a loop with proper phrasing and muting; make use of backing track context.
tracks.rationale: Progresses from loop construction to authentic blues improvisation, incorporating pentatonic shapes, backing track context, and voice-leading within the blues framework.

tracks.name: Complete loop flow: rhythm + lead chain
tracks.identity_statement: I orchestrate a full looping performance: rhythm and lead loops; playback; safety; analysis; and performance readiness.
tracks.intended_outcome: Complete loop performance: rhythm + lead chain; playback; and reflective practice to improve timing and dynamics.
tracks.rationale: Consolidates foundational skills into a full, performable loop chain, with emphasis on dynamics, safety, performance readiness, and post-practice analysis.

sequencing_rationale: Begin with foundational technique and pentatonic mapping to ensure clean fretting and reliable navigation of the fretboard.
Introduce loop mechanics and timing alignment for a stable backing context before adding melodic content.
Progress to blues improvisation within a looping context, emphasizing phrasing, key stability, and voice-leading.
Culminate in a full loop performance that integrates rhythm, lead, safety, and reflective analysis.
pacing_rationale: 8-week horizon with 30 minutes/day necessitates gradual milestones: early weeks solidify technique and patterns; mid weeks integrate looping with blues; final weeks consolidate into a performable loop chain and self-review.

Branching allows a learner to deepen either the blues- improvisation track or the complete loop performance track after establishing core skills, ensuring meaningful progression rather than arbitrary difficulty.
assumptions: Practices 30 minutes per day, 5 days per week, for 8 weeks.
Access to a loop pedal capable of recording, overdubbing, and playback.
Standard tuning and basic amp settings assumed.
Practice environment allows use of a metronome.
No external performance requirement during the horizon.
